memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'The priest is to make atonement for the whole Israelite community, and they will be forgiven, for it was not intentional and they have presented to the Lord for their wrong a food offering and a sin offering. The whole Israelite community and the foreigners residing among them will be forgiven, because all the people were involved in the unintentional wrong.'" — Num 15:25-26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"They will be forgiven." What sweeter words could there be? After the offering was made, the result was certain: forgiveness. God did not leave His people in doubt about their standing. When atonement was made in the way He appointed, forgiveness was sure.

And notice again the beautiful inclusion: "the foreigners residing among them will be forgiven" too. The mercy extended to everyone within the community, native and stranger alike. God's forgiveness was never a stingy trickle for the privileged few, but a flowing river for all who came to Him rightly.

There is enormous assurance in this for us. God wants His people to know they are forgiven — not to hope so, not to guess so, but to know it. Faith is not meant to live in constant uncertainty about whether we are accepted. When atonement has been made, forgiveness is real and settled.

For us, the atonement is not a bull and a goat but the Lamb of God, Jesus Christ. His sacrifice was offered once for all, and it accomplished everything. Because of Him, we can say with confidence, "I am forgiven." Not because our offering was good enough, but because His was. This assurance is not presumption; it is simply trusting what God has said. If you have come to God through Christ, you may rest in these words: you will be forgiven — indeed, you are.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you live in assurance of forgiveness, or in constant uncertainty?
2. Why can you be confident of forgiveness through Christ's sacrifice?
3. How does the inclusion of the foreigner encourage you about God's welcome?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that forgiveness through Christ is sure and settled, not a matter of guesswork. Help me to rest in the finished work of Jesus and to know, with confidence, that I am forgiven. Thank You for Your welcoming, abundant mercy. Amen.
